linear guards this bare-name alias with `!prefer_bound_call`, which is what keeps a user's own binding of the same name from being hijacked into the builtin (#832: an arity-mismatched hijack read past `args` and trapped the compiler itself). The gc lane has no prefer_bound_call -- `source_is_bound` in gc/backend_call.vibe only picks the alias spelling, it does not skip the builtin chain -- so a gc arm would reintroduce that hijack. Not a codegen gap (#1861)

#1015: gc/backend_call.vibe matches this callsite arm via a literal `fname == "to_string"` (safe here -- the gc lane compiles one self-contained file at a time, so no other file's own "to_string" export can collide, unlike linear's multi-file merge); the linear lane serves the equivalent call-site fast path in expr/compile_call.vibe too, but keyed off `fname == namespace_exported_name(...)`, a COMPUTED string, not a literal `fname == "..."` match -- invisible to this script's regex extraction, so linear does not appear as a served name for "to_string" even though it handles the same case
